# QDEF — Quick Data Exchange Format (full reference)

QDEF is a binary container format for multi-action 2D barcodes (QR, Data Matrix, Aztec). It carries typed, self-describing records in a compact CBOR-based wire format.

## Wire format

4-byte magic: `51 44 45 46` ("QDEF"), followed by the root Record. An application carrying QDEF content under its own URI scheme (`myapp:...`) skips the magic — the scheme prefix already identifies the payload. Every other carrier always includes it.

Record: `[namespace?, ns_annotation?, typeId*, type_annotation?, map?, subrecord*]`

| Slot | CBOR type | Description |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| namespace | bstr (major 2), non-empty | Optional. Cascades to subrecords only — never scopes this Record's own typeId. Empty bstr (h'') is not a valid token. |
| ns_annotation | tstr (major 3) | Optional. Only after namespace. Human-readable label. |
| typeId | int(s), first may be negative (major 0 or 1) | Optional consecutive integers. Absent = Bundle. First element's sign decides scope (see Namespace below); every element after it is a plain uint. `1`-`22` = standard types. |
| type_annotation | tstr (major 3) | Optional. Only after typeId. Human-readable label. |
| map | map (major 5) | Optional field map. Key 0 = payload. |
| subrecords | array(s) (major 4) | Remaining arrays, each a nested Record. |

A bare tstr anywhere else (no preceding bstr or ints) is malformed.

## Map keys

| Key | Purpose | Governance |
|-----|---------|------------|
| 0 | Payload | RESERVED — same meaning in every Record |
| 1 | Payload descriptor | RESERVED — optional hint, never load-bearing |
| -1 | Record ID | Spec-reserved — bstr or tstr correlation token; UUID MUST use CBOR tag 37 |
| <= -2 | Future common headers | Standards Action only, not app-allocated — even/odd criticality pre-reserved |
| >= 2 | Type-specific | Per-Type, even=critical, odd=optional |

## Standard types (global, no namespace, numbers 1-22)

| TypeId | Name | Key 0 | Key 1 |
|--------|------|-------|-------|
| [1] | Split | fragment bytes | — |
| [2] | Encrypt | ciphertext + tag | — |
| [3] | Media Payload | content bytes | media type (MIME/CoAP) |
| [4] | Compress | deflated bytes | — |
| [5] | Open/Hint URI | URI | label |
| [6] | App Route | domain/hash | label |
| [7] | Media Preview | — (content in subrecord) | — |
| [8] | Signature | signature bytes | — |

## Namespace

A namespace bstr's job is always to become the ambient namespace for whatever's nested inside that Record — unconditional, regardless of that Record's own typeId. Whether it *also* scopes the Record carrying it is decided purely by that typeId's own sign:

- **Non-negative typeId** = global, unconditionally. Same meaning to every decoder regardless of any namespace bstr present or any ambient flowing through.
- **Negative typeId** = scoped. Adopts this Record's own namespace bstr if it carries one — a Record MAY simultaneously introduce a fresh namespace and be scoped by it, in one array, no second Record needed. Otherwise adopts the ambient namespace received from an ancestor Record.

Namespace value is self-chosen via SHA-256 hash of a reverse-domain string, truncated to 4+ bytes. A namespace's own type numbering (e.g. a registry's ScopedTypeId) is always a positive declared magnitude; the wire-encoded sign is a separate, encode-time decision, not part of the type's identity — negate the magnitude to encode it scoped.

Namespace must be transmitted in-band, never implied by carrier context — a Record with no namespace bstr anywhere in its ancestry is unconditionally global/standard typeId space.

## Bundle

No typeId. MAY carry a namespace bstr (to cascade to subrecords) and/or a map with only a Record ID (key -1) — MUST NOT carry key 0 or key 1. Subrecords carry the actual content.

## Annotations

Optional text strings in two positions: after namespace (ns_annotation) and after typeId (type_annotation). Human-readable labels, never load-bearing for routing. A decoder MUST preserve but MUST NOT use for any parse-time decision.

## Criticality

Positive keys >= 2 (Type-scoped) and negative keys <= -2 (Standards Action-governed) both have even/odd criticality. Even = unrecognized key aborts that Record. Odd = unrecognized key silently ignored. Keys 0 (payload), 1 (descriptor), and -1 (Record ID) are fixed, spec-reserved, and excluded from this rule.

## Canonical encoding

Encoders MUST produce CBOR meeting RFC 8949 §4.2.1 core deterministic encoding: shortest-form integers, definite-length items only, map keys sorted by their own encoded bytes (shorter first, then bytewise — NOT plain integer value, since a negative key's encoded byte is always larger than a same-magnitude non-negative key's).

## Full spec

https://qdef-format.github.io/spec.html
